cve_summary: arch/x86/kvm/emulate.c in the KVM subsystem in the Linux kernel through 3.17.2 does not properly perform RIP changes, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (guest OS crash) via a crafted application.
commit_message:
KVM: x86: Handle errors when RIP is set during far jumps

Far jmp/call/ret may fault while loading a new RIP.  Currently KVM does not
handle this case, and may result in failed vm-entry once the assignment is
done.  The tricky part of doing so is that loading the new CS affects the
VMCS/VMCB state, so if we fail during loading the new RIP, we are left in
unconsistent state.  Therefore, this patch saves on 64-bit the old CS
descriptor and restores it if loading RIP failed.

This fixes CVE-2014-3647.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Nadav Amit <namit@cs.technion.ac.il>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: Loads the state from a 32-bit Task State Segment (TSS) into the x86 emulation context.

Parameters:
ctxt (struct x86_emulate_ctxt *): Pointer to the emulation context that holds CPU state.
tss (struct tss_segment_32 *): Pointer to the TSS structure containing the state to load.

Returns: int: Returns X86EMUL_CONTINUE on success or an error code if a fault occurs during loading.

Logic: The function first sets the control register CR3 from the TSS and updates the instruction pointer and flags. It then writes the general-purpose registers from the TSS values. Segment selectors are loaded before segment descriptors, with special handling for Protected Mode and VM86 mode switching. The function attempts to load each segment descriptor (LDT, ES, CS, SS, DS, FS, GS) and checks for faults, returning an error code if any occur. If all operations succeed, it returns X86EMUL_CONTINUE.
"""
